::: {.rule-label}
About
:::

::: {.prose}
I am a survey methodologist working at the intersection of measurement science, probability sampling, and applied data science. My research training comes through the **University of Maryland Joint Program in Survey Methodology (JPSM)** and the **University of Michigan Survey Research Center**, where I earned an **MS in Survey and Data Science**; I also hold an **MA in Psychology**.

My work spans probability sample design, latent variable modeling, multilevel and Bayesian methods, and the responsible integration of machine learning and large language models into survey research workflows. My methodological foundation rests on the **Total Survey Error (TSE) framework** developed by Groves and colleagues, extended through the **Total Error Framework (TEF)** of Amaya, Biemer, and Kinyon (2020), which adapts TSE to non-probability and Big Data sources such as social media, administrative records, and AI-generated content. This dual foundation lets me reason about data quality consistently across traditional surveys and the alternative data streams that increasingly supplement them. The [methods atlas](methods.html) lays that foundation out interactively.

I am especially interested in questions about measurement validity (how new tools affect what we are actually measuring) and in building reproducible, transparent analytic pipelines that make methodological decisions easy to audit.

Most of what you'll find here is built in **R**, organized around the tidyverse, and rendered through **Quarto** and **Shiny**. I favor functional code, fully reproducible pipelines, and methods documentation that travels with the code.
:::
